## IMC data 

### Tumor panel 

#### Preprocessing 

```{r}
tumor_key <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/tumor_panel/data_analysis/tumor_key_features.csv")

# Preprocessing as suggested by Boeva (Cell Reports Methods)
# Step 1: Only keep columns with less than 10% of NA values 
## This often removes INT values
remove <- colnames(tumor_key)[colMeans(is.na(tumor_key)) > 0.1]
remove <- remove[!remove %in% c("status_OS", "OS_months")]

tumor_selected <- tumor_key %>% select(-remove)

# Step 2: Missing numerical values can be imputed (Median across non-missing samples OR minimum for INT values)

summary(is.na(tumor_selected))
min(tumor_selected$INT_TU_HLADRhi__CD8_T_cell, na.rm = TRUE)

tumor_selected[] <- lapply(colnames(tumor_selected), function(colname) {
  if (colname %in% c("status_OS", "OS_months")) {
    return(tumor_selected[[colname]])  
  } else {
    # If column has NA and is not excluded, replace NA with column minimum
    col <- tumor_selected[[colname]]
    if (any(is.na(col)) & str_detect(colname, "INT")) {
      col[is.na(col)] <- min(col, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
    return(col)
  }
})

summary(is.na(tumor_selected))

# Add specific prefix
colnames(tumor_selected)[4:ncol(tumor_selected)] <- paste0("IMC_TU_",colnames(tumor_selected)[4:ncol(tumor_selected)])
```

Save 

```{r}
write_csv(tumor_selected, "/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/tumor_panel/data_analysis/tumor_key_features_processed.csv")
```

Add to general metadata

```{r}
for (entry in colnames(tumor_selected)[2:ncol(tumor_selected)]) {
  metadata_general[,entry] <- tumor_selected[,entry][match(metadata_general[,"PID"],tumor_selected[,"PID"])]
}





```

## Perform BlockForest

### Simple

```{r}
set.seed(22)
# Train the blockForest model
blockforobj <- blockfor(x_train, as.matrix(y_train), 
                        blocks = block,
                        splitrule = "extratrees", block.method = "BlockForest",
                        always.select.block = 1, importance = "permutation")
    
# Make predictions on the test data
predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = x_test, block.method = "BlockForest")
```

```{r}
concordance(Surv(y_test$OS_months, y_test$status_OS) ~ rowSums(predres$survival), timewt="n/G2")
```

```{r}
scale(blockforobj$forest$variable.importance)
```






### 5fold CV (Outer)

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(blockForest)
library(survival)

# Create a function for 5 fold outer cross-validation
cross_validate_blockforest <- function(x, y, folds, block) {
  results <- vector("list", length(folds))
  
  for (i in seq_along(folds)) {
    
    # Split the data into training and test sets
    x_train <- x[folds[[i]],]
    x_test <- x[-folds[[i]],]

    y_train <- y[folds[[i]],]
    y_test <- y[-folds[[i]],]
    
    # Train the blockForest model
    blockforobj <- blockfor(X = x_train, 
                            y = as.matrix(y_train), 
                            blocks = block,
                            splitrule = "extratrees", 
                            block.method = "BlockForest",
                            #always.select.block = 1,
                            importance = "permutation")
    
    # Make predictions on the test data
    predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = x_test)
    
    # Store the results for evaluation, e.g., store predicted survival functions
    results[[i]] <- list(predictions = predres, 
                         actual_surv = y_test, 
                         variable_importance = blockforobj$forest$variable.importance)
  }
  
  return(results)
}
```

```{r}
# Create x and y 
metadata_select <- metadata_general %>% select(PID, OS_months, status_OS, age, gender, pT_combined, ISUP_combined, necrose) %>% filter(complete.cases(.))

# # Encode as binary

# metadata_select$ISUP_combined <- ifelse(metadata_select$ISUP_combined == "1/2", 0, 1)

# metadata_select$age

metadata_select$ISUP_combined <- factor(metadata_select$ISUP_combined, levels = sort(unique(metadata_select$ISUP_combined)))
metadata_select$necrose <- factor(metadata_select$necrose, levels = sort(unique(metadata_select$necrose)))
metadata_select$gender <- factor(metadata_select$gender, levels = sort(unique(metadata_select$gender)))

y <- metadata_select %>% column_to_rownames("PID") %>% select(OS_months, status_OS)

x <- metadata_select %>% column_to_rownames("PID") %>% select(-status_OS)
colnames(x) <- paste0("CLIN_", colnames(x))
```

### Integrated Brier Score

TO BE UPDATED

```{r}
library(SurvMetrics)

# Define time of interest
## Option 1: Use times of actual events in test data
IBSrange <- sort(ysurvtest[,1][ysurvtest[,2] == 1])

## Option 2: Generate 100 uniformly spaced points within the time range (min, 0.9 quantile) of the test data
IBSrange <- seq(min(y_test[,1]), quantile(y_test[,1], 0.9), length.out = 100)

SurvMetrics::IBS(Surv(y_test[,1], y_test[,2]), predres$survival, IBSrange = c(1,80))
```

```{r}
ibs_scores <- sapply(cv_results, function(res) {
  IBS(Surv(res$actual[, 1], res$actual[, 2]), res$predictions$survival)
})

ibs_scores_1 <- sapply(cv_results_1, function(res) {
  IBS(Surv(res$actual[, 1], res$actual[, 2]), res$predictions$survival)
})

# Compare two models
out <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, ibs_scores = ibs_scores, model = "test")
out_1 <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, ibs_scores = ibs_scores_1, model = "test_1")

plot <- rbind(out, out_1)

ggplot(plot, aes(x = model, y = ibs_scores, fill = model))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = NA)+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,0.3))+
  theme_classic()+
  stat_compare_means()
```

```{r}
})

})

# Compare two models

out_1 <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, concordance_scores = concordance_scores_1, model = "test_1")
```

### Kaplan-Meier and risk group definition

```{r}
dataset <- cv_results
surv_plots <- list()
data_out <- list()

for(i in seq_along(dataset)){
  res <- dataset[[i]]
  out <- cbind(res$actual_surv,chf = rowSums(res$predictions$chf))
  out_df <- out %>% mutate(risk_group = ifelse(chf > median(chf), "high", "low"), fold = i) %>% rownames_to_column("PID")

  #Plot specific survival curves
  fit <- survfit(Surv(out_df$OS_months, out_df$status_OS) ~ risk_group, data = out_df)

  surv_plots[[i]] <- fit
  data_out[[i]] <- out_df
}

# Plot all curves for each CV fold
ggsurvplot_list(surv_plots, 
                data = data_out,
                risk.table = TRUE, # Add risk table
                risk.table.col = "strata", # Change risk table color by groups
                linetype = "strata", # Change line type by groups
                surv.median.line = "hv", # Specify median survival
                ggtheme = theme_classic(), # Change ggplot2 theme
                palette = "Set1",
                conf.int = TRUE
                )

## Pick a specific fold
ggsurvplot(surv_plots[[2]], 
          pval = TRUE,
          risk.table = TRUE, # Add risk table
          risk.table.col = "strata", # Change risk table color by groups
          linetype = "strata", # Change line type by groups
          surv.median.line = "hv", # Specify median survival
          ggtheme = theme_classic(), # Change ggplot2 theme
          palette = "Set1",
          conf.int = TRUE
)

# Display averaged chf across all folds
data_comb <- do.call("rbind", data_out)

data_comb <- data_comb %>% group_by(PID) %>% mutate(mean_chf = mean(chf)) %>% select(PID, OS_months, status_OS, mean_chf) %>% unique() %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(risk_group = ifelse(mean_chf > median(mean_chf), "high", "low"))

fit <- survfit(Surv(data_comb$OS_months, data_comb$status_OS) ~ risk_group, data = data_comb)

ggsurvplot(fit, 
          pval = TRUE,
          risk.table = TRUE, # Add risk table
          risk.table.col = "strata", # Change risk table color by groups
          linetype = "strata", # Change line type by groups
          surv.median.line = "hv", # Specify median survival
          ggtheme = theme_classic(), # Change ggplot2 theme
          palette = "Set1",
          conf.int = TRUE
)
```

### Importance

#### Feature-level

```{r}
variable_importance <- blockforobj$forest$variable.importance

# Calculate block-wise aggregated importance
aggregate_importance <- sapply(block, function(indices) {
  mean(variable_importance[indices])  # Mean importance of variables in each block
})
names(aggregate_importance) <- paste("Block", 1:length(block), sep="_")
aggregate_importance
```


```{r}
variable_importance <- sapply(cv_results_1, function(res) {

# Potentially scale / min-max normalize
plot <- variable_importance %>% as.data.frame %>% rownames_to_column("feature") %>% pivot_longer(2:ncol(.),names_to = "fold", values_to = "importance") 

ggplot(plot, aes(x = feature, y = importance, fill = feature))+
```
